title: Walk-animation phase must advance with bomber velocity, not wall-clock
intent: Shipped walk-swing animation in `bench-animation-system.ts` and consumed by the production `kaboom.bomber-animation-driver` advances its sine-wave phase off `BenchAnimationState.elapsed` — pure wall-clock. Result: a bomber on easy-difficulty preset (GridMover.speed = 2) animates at the SAME stride frequency as a hard-difficulty bomber (speed = 4). Two bombers with different Speed-Up power-up counts also stride identically. This breaks the readability link between movement speed and visual motion: the player can't see 'this bot moves slower than me' from the animation alone. The animation phase must be locked to TRAVELLED DISTANCE per fixedUpdate (Δphase = Δposition_magnitude × strideFrequencyPerCell), so slow bombers visibly take slow strides and fast bombers visibly hustle. Pure presentation fix — zero gameplay impact, zero performance cost. This was specified in GDP-2026-05-20-009 acceptance hints AND in GDP-2026-05-22-002 acceptance hints ('Phase advances with travelled distance, NOT wall-clock'), but slipped through both implementations.
rationale: Sources: `docs/game-design/characters-and-visual.md` §3.3 (the walk-cycle bullet — 'Phase advances with movement velocity, not wall clock — slow-walking bot animates slowly'), GDP-2026-05-20-009 acceptance hints (same line), GDP-2026-05-22-002 acceptance hints (same line). The constraint was always part of the design but never landed in code; this story is its corrective ticket. Locking walk phase to velocity is the single most important readability connection between gameplay state (BomberStats.speed, Speed-Up pickups, difficulty preset) and the on-screen body — without it, players can't read 'I'm faster than them' from looking.
acceptanceHints: Investigation entry point: `examples/procbomber-bench/src/systems/bench-animation-system.ts` lines 81–125 — every walk-related pure helper (walkSwingX, walkSwingKneeElbow, walkRootBobY) currently uses `elapsed` directly. `examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/bomber-animation-driver.ts` decides walk-swing kind but doesn't override the phase source.

DESIGN INTENT: walk-swing phase = ∫(velocity × strideFrequencyPerCell) dt. When velocity = 0, phase HOLDS (does not advance). When velocity = 1 cell/sec, phase advances at strideFrequencyPerCell × 2π radians per second. Default strideFrequencyPerCell = ~0.8 strides per cell (one full step covers ~1.25 cells of travel — feels natural at toy scale).
RECOMMENDED IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE (dev's call on exact factoring):

Option A — extend BenchAnimationState with a separate `walkPhase: number` field. The kaboom bomber-animation-driver writes `walkPhase += velocity_magnitude × strideFrequencyPerCell × dt` every fixedUpdate when kind = 'walk-swing'. The pure helpers (walkSwingX, walkSwingKneeElbow, walkRootBobY) take `walkPhase` instead of `elapsed`. Bench-only contexts that don't have a GridMover keep wall-clock fallback: walkPhase += dt × DEFAULT_FALLBACK_FREQ.

Option B — keep walkSwingX(elapsed, ...) signature; driver overwrites BenchAnimationState.elapsed each fixedUpdate to be a velocity-integrated value instead of wall-clock. Less clean (overloads the meaning of `elapsed`) but minimal diff.
Recommend Option A. Bench preview without a GridMover still works; production locks to velocity.

VELOCITY SOURCE: GridMover already carries the per-tick movement. Read its currentLerp delta OR sample world-space Transform.position delta between consecutive fixedUpdates. Either works deterministically.

IDLE-BOB STAYS WALL-CLOCK: idle bobble is presentational breathing, not stride; it ticks at the same frequency regardless of any gameplay state. Only `walk-swing` (shoulders, hips, knees, elbows, rootBobY) phase-locks to velocity.
REACH animation (place-bomb IK burst) — STAYS wall-clock. It's a 0.4 s discrete burst, not a cyclic motion.
DEATH / RAGDOLL — already physics-driven from S105+S108, untouched.
ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST:

Load /?project=kaboom-crew&difficulty=easy → bot.1 has GridMover.speed = 2 → bot's walk-cycle frequency is visibly slower than at &difficulty=hard (speed = 4). Player's stride speed scales with collected Speed-Up power-ups in the same way.
A bomber stopped at a wall (collision keeps velocity_magnitude ≈ 0) → walk-cycle FREEZES at its current phase, doesn't continue swinging in place.
A bomber starting to move from rest → walk-cycle starts smoothly from its frozen phase, no snap.
UNIT TESTS:
walkSwingX(phase=0) → 0 (rest pose).
walkSwingX(phase=π) → opposite-sign extreme (one stride forward).
Phase integration: 10 ticks at dt=1/60 with velocity_magnitude = 2 → phase = 2 × 0.8 × 10/60 × 2π = ~1.676 rad. Floating-point tolerant assertion.
Velocity = 0 → phase unchanged across N ticks.
Bench fallback (no GridMover available): phase advances at DEFAULT_FALLBACK_FREQ rate so the bench preview still demonstrates walk-cycle motion without gameplay state.

DETERMINISM: phase integration is purely a function of (velocity_magnitude per tick, dt, strideFrequencyPerCell, prior phase) — all deterministic. Bot-vs-bot regression test outputs unchanged in gameplay; visual replay differs only in stride timing (acceptable per visual-determinism-is-non-binding rule in gameplay-systems.md §12.1).
DOCS UPDATES (in this story's PR):
characters-and-visual.md §3.3 walk-cycle bullet — reinforce the rule, point at this story.
gameplay-systems.md §2.2 — add an explicit 'animation phase locks to velocity' line under Movement rules so future stories don't repeat the slip.
OUT OF SCOPE (explicit):
Per-bomber stride frequency variation (could come from recipe.proportions.legLength — short legs = faster cadence, long legs = slower — but defer to a follow-up if it matters visually).
Foot-plant ground constraint (already deferred S104 per S103 notes — depends on hip-Y compensation via the IK solver).
Arm swing decoupling from leg swing (currently arms mirror legs in counter-phase — the canonical walk-cycle pattern; intentional).
